chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said:
Al-Zahaar does not occur upon anger.

key_terms.الظِّهَارُ: Zahaar, a form of divorce in Islamic jurisprudence where a husband declares his wife's back to be like his mother's back.
key_terms.الْغَضَبِ: Anger, a state of emotional agitation that can affect legal intent.

ai.seo_question: Does Zahaar take effect if pronounced in anger?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the declaration of Zahaar is not automatically effective when pronounced in a state of anger, emphasizing the necessity of composure and intent for legal validity. This ruling aligns with the broader Shia jurisprudential principle that emotional agitation can negate the immediate legal impact of certain verbal acts, ensuring fairness in marital disputes. The hadith underscores the importance of deliberate intent (niyyah) in applying this specific form of marital separation.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, 
(It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Zahaar does not occur upon the anger’.
en.sarwar: 25. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr who has said the following: “Al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Al-Zihar (calling one’s wife as one’s mother) does not take place upon anger (if expressed because of anger).”’
